1	# @gravity-ui/table documentation
2	
3	Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/table`.
4	Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth.
5	
6	Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/table/build/docs/`).
7	
8	## For AI agents
9	
10	A headless, TanStack-Table-powered data grid for Gravity UI apps — reach for it for sortable, selectable, groupable, reorderable, and virtualized tables instead of composing raw markup on top of uikit's basic `Table`.
11	
12	### When to use
13	
14	- Large datasets that need row or window virtualization (`useRowVirtualizer`, `useWindowRowVirtualizer`).
15	- Column sorting, resizing, reordering (`ColumnReorderingProvider`), pinning, and per-user column settings (`TableSettings`).
16	- Row selection (single/multi, ranged) and tree/grouped rows with expandable cells.
17	
18	### When not to use
19	
20	- A simple, static table with a handful of rows and no advanced features — uikit's built-in `Table` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit) is lighter.
21	- A non-tabular list — use `List` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
22	- Spreadsheet-style inline cell editing — this grid is read/display-focused, not an editable spreadsheet.
23	
24	### Common pitfalls
25	
26	- **You build the table with `useTable`, then render `<Table table={table} />`.** The main prop is `table` (the instance), not `data`/`columns` directly on `<Table>`; pass `data` and `columns` to `useTable`.
27	- **Types come from the `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack` subpath.** Import `ColumnDef`, `RowSelectionState`, `SortingState`, etc. from `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack`, not from the package root.
28	- **Sorting needs an accessor.** A column must have `accessorKey`/`accessorFn` for sorting to work; set `enableSorting` and provide `getRowId`.
29	- **React 19 + React Compiler can skip re-renders.** This is an upstream TanStack Table issue — add the `'use no memo'` directive to the component or memoize `data`.
30	- **Range selection breaks with nested rows.** Ranged selection is undefined behavior when the table has grouped/nested rows; use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` for correct parent-checkbox state with grouping.
31	
32	## Install
33	
34	```shell
35	npm install --save @gravity-ui/table
36	```
37	
38	## Usage
39	
40	```tsx
41	import React from 'react';
42	import {Table, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
43	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
44	
45	interface Person {
46	  id: string;
47	  name: string;
48	  age: number;
49	}
50	
51	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
52	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 100},
53	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
54	];
55	
56	const data: Person[] = [
57	  {id: 'name', name: 'John', age: 23},
58	  {id: 'age', name: 'Michael', age: 27},
59	];
60	
61	const BasicExample = () => {
62	  const table = useTable({
63	    columns,
64	    data,
65	  });
66	
67	  return <Table table={table} />;
68	};
69	```
70	
71	### Components
72	
73	There are two Table components that you can use:
74	
75	- `BaseTable` - a component with basic styles only;
76	- `Table` - a component with Gravity UI based styles.
77	
78	#### Row selection
79	
80	```tsx
81	import {selectionColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
82	import type {RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
83	
84	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
85	  selectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
86	  // ...other columns
87	];
88	
89	const data: Person[] = [
90	  /* ... */
91	];
92	
93	const RowSelectionExample = () => {
94	  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = React.useState<RowSelectionState>({});
95	
96	  const table = useTable({
97	    columns,
98	    data,
99	    enableRowSelection: true,
100	    enableMultiRowSelection: true,
101	    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
102	    state: {
103	      rowSelection,
104	    },
105	  });
106	
107	  return <Table table={table} />;
108	};
109	```
110	
111	To use grouping with selection, use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong. https://github.com/TanStack/table/issues/4878
112	
113	#### Custom Ranged Selection Column
114	
115	The `useToggleRangeSelectionHandler` hook returns a change handler that listens for Shift+click events and performs ranged row selection. It needs to be passed a `CellContext` instance in order to have access to the table's and row's internal states.
116	
117	```tsx
118	import React, {type ChangeEvent, useCallback, useState} from 'react';
119	
120	import {Table, useToggleRangeSelectionHandler, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
121	import type {CellContext, ColumnDef, RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
122	import {Checkbox, type CheckboxProps} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
123	
124	type CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps = Omit<CheckboxProps, 'onChange'> & {
125	  cellContext: CellContext<unknown, unknown>;
126	};
127	
128	const CustomRangedSelectionCheckbox = ({
129	  className,
130	  cellContext,
131	  ...restProps
132	}: CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps) => {
133	  const rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler = useToggleRangeSelectionHandler(cellContext);
134	
135	  const handleChange = useCallback(
136	    (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void => {
137	      rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler(event);
138	    },
139	    [rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler],
140	  );
141	
142	  return <Checkbox {...restProps} onChange={handleChange} />;
143	};
144	
145	const customSelectionColumn: ColumnDef<unknown> = {
146	  id: '_select',
147	  header: ({table}) => (
148	    <Checkbox
149	      size="l"
150	      checked={table.getIsAllRowsSelected()}
151	      indeterminate={table.getIsSomeRowsSelected()}
152	      onChange={table.getToggleAllRowsSelectedHandler()}
153	    />
154	  ),
155	  cell: (cellContext) => (
156	    <CustomRangedSelectionCheckbox
157	      size="l"
158	      checked={cellContext.row.getIsSelected()}
159	      disabled={!cellContext.row.getCanSelect()}
160	      indeterminate={cellContext.row.getIsSomeSelected()}
161	      cellContext={cellContext}
162	    />
163	  ),
164	  size: 41,
165	  maxSize: 41,
166	  minSize: 41,
167	  enableResizing: false,
168	  enableSorting: false,
169	};
170	
171	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
172	  customSelectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
173	  // ...other columns
174	];
175	
176	const data: Person[] = [
177	  /* ... */
178	];
179	
180	const RowRangedSelectionExample = () => {
181	  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({});
182	
183	  const table = useTable({
184	    columns,
185	    data,
186	    enableRowSelection: true,
187	    enableMultiRowSelection: true,
188	    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
189	    state: {
190	      rowSelection,
191	    },
192	  });
193	
194	  return <Table table={table} />;
195	};
196	```
197	
198	There is also a `RangedSelectionCheckbox` component, which internally uses the hook and accepts a `CellContext` instance as a prop. This component provides a shorthand for adding ranged selection functionality to custom selection columns.
199	
200	```tsx
201	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
202	import {RangedSelectionCheckbox, SelectionCheckbox} from '@gravity-ui/table';
203	
204	export const selectionColumn: ColumnDef<unknown> = {
205	  id: '_select',
206	  header: ({table}) => (
207	    <SelectionCheckbox
208	      checked={table.getIsAllRowsSelected()}
209	      disabled={!table.options.enableRowSelection}
210	      indeterminate={table.getIsSomeRowsSelected()}
211	      onChange={table.getToggleAllRowsSelectedHandler()}
212	    />
213	  ),
214	  cell: (cellContext) => (
215	    <RangedSelectionCheckbox
216	      checked={cellContext.row.getIsSelected()}
217	      disabled={!cellContext.row.getCanSelect()}
218	      indeterminate={cellContext.row.getIsSomeSelected()}
219	      cellContext={cellContext}
220	    />
221	  ),
222	  meta: {
223	    hideInSettings: true,
224	  },
225	  size: 32,
226	  minSize: 32,
227	};
228	```
229	
230	By default, the selection column generated with `selectionColumn` includes ranged selection functionality.
231	
232	```tsx
233	import {selectionColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
234	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
235	
236	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
237	  selectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
238	  // ...other columns
239	];
240	```
241	
242	**Note**: If the table contains nested rows, range selection will not work. At the moment, this is considered undefined behavior.
243	
244	#### Sorting
245	
246	Learn about the column properties in the react-table [docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/guide/sorting)
247	
248	```tsx
249	import type {SortingState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
250	
251	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
252	  /* ... */
253	];
254	
255	const data: Person[] = [
256	  /* ... */
257	];
258	
259	const SortingExample = () => {
260	  const [sorting, setSorting] = React.useState<SortingState>([]);
261	
262	  // Your column MUST have accessorFn for sorting to be enabled
263	
264	  const table = useTable({
265	    columns,
266	    data,
267	    enableSorting: true,
268	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
269	    onSortingChange: setSorting,
270	    state: {
271	      sorting,
272	    },
273	  });
274	
275	  return <Table table={table} />;
276	};
277	```
278	
279	If you want to sort the elements manually pass `manualSorting` property:
280	
281	```tsx
282	const table = useTable({
283	  // ...
284	  manualSorting: true,
285	});
286	```
287	
288	#### Grouping
289	
290	```tsx
291	import type {ExpandedState, Row} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
292	
293	interface Person {
294	  id: string;
295	  name: string;
296	  age: number;
297	}
298	
299	interface PersonGroup {
300	  id: string;
301	  name: string;
302	  items: Person[];
303	}
304	
305	type Item = PersonGroup | Person;
306	
307	const columns: ColumnDef<Item>[] = [
308	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 200},
309	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
310	];
311	
312	const data: Item[] = [
313	  {
314	    id: 'friends',
315	    name: 'Friends',
316	    items: [
317	      {id: 'nick', name: 'Nick', age: 25},
318	      {id: 'tom', name: 'Tom', age: 21},
319	    ],
320	  },
321	  {
322	    id: 'relatives',
323	    name: 'Relatives',
324	    items: [
325	      {id: 'john', name: 'John', age: 23},
326	      {id: 'michael', name: 'Michael', age: 27},
327	    ],
328	  },
329	];
330	
331	const getGroupTitle = (row: Row<Item>) => row.getValue<string>('name');
332	
333	const GroupingExample = () => {
334	  const [expanded, setExpanded] = React.useState<ExpandedState>({});
335	
336	  const table = useTable({
337	    columns,
338	    data,
339	    enableExpanding: true,
340	    getSubRows: (item) => ('items' in item ? item.items : undefined),
341	    onExpandedChange: setExpanded,
342	    state: {
343	      expanded,
344	    },
345	  });
346	
347	  return <Table table={table} getGroupTitle={getGroupTitle} />;
348	};
349	```
350	
351	To use grouping with selection, use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong. https://github.com/TanStack/table/issues/4878
352	
353	To enable nesting styles, pass `withNestingStyles = true` in the column configuration.
354	
355	Nesting indicators can be disabled by passing `showTreeDepthIndicators = false`.
356	
357	To add a control for expanding/collapsing rows, wrap the cell content with the `TreeExpandableCell` component or with your similar custom component:
358	
359	```tsx
360	import {TreeExpandableCell} from '@gravity-ui/table';
361	
362	const columns: ColumnDef<Item>[] = [
363	  {
364	    accessorKey: 'name',
365	    header: 'Name',
366	    size: 200,
367	    showTreeDepthIndicators: false,
368	    withNestingStyles: true,
369	    cell: ({row, info}) => (
370	      <TreeExpandableCell row={row}>{info.getValue<string>()}</TreeExpandableCell>
371	    ),
372	  },
373	  // ...other columns
374	];
375	```
376	
377	#### Reordering
378	
379	```tsx
380	import type {ReorderingProviderProps} from '@gravity-ui/table';
381	import {dragHandleColumn, ReorderingProvider} from '@gravity-ui/table';
382	
383	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
384	  dragHandleColumn,
385	  // ...other columns
386	];
387	
388	const data: Person[] = [
389	  /* ... */
390	];
391	
392	const ReorderingExample = () => {
393	  const table = useTable({
394	    columns,
395	    data,
396	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
397	  });
398	
399	  const handleReorder = React.useCallback<
400	    NonNullable<ReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
401	  >(
402	    ({
403	      draggedItemKey,
404	      targetItemKey,
405	      baseItemKey,
406	      baseNextItemKey,
407	      enableNesting,
408	      nextChild,
409	      pullFromParent,
410	    }) => {
411	      // ...
412	    },
413	    [],
414	  );
415	
416	  return (
417	    <ReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleReorder}>
418	      <Table table={table} />
419	    </ReorderingProvider>
420	  );
421	};
422	```
423	
424	#### Reordering without a drag handle
425	
426	Set `dragWithoutHandle` to use the whole row as the drag activator and omit
427	`dragHandleColumn` from the column definitions:
428	
429	```tsx
430	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
431	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
432	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
433	];
434	
435	return (
436	  <ReorderingProvider table={table} dragWithoutHandle onReorder={handleReorder}>
437	    <Table table={table} />
438	  </ReorderingProvider>
439	);
440	```
441	
442	The pointer must move by 8 pixels before dragging starts, so regular row and control clicks keep
443	working. To exclude a custom part of a row from starting a drag, call `preventDefault()` in its
444	`onPointerDown` handler.
445	
446	`ReorderingProvider` enables dnd-kit's vertical auto-scroll by default. Pass `autoScroll={false}`
447	when the application supplies its own drag auto-scroll implementation; running both at once can
448	produce competing scroll writes.
449	
450	Custom drag handles should read `attributes`, `listeners`, and `setActivatorNodeRef` from
451	`DraggableRowContext` and attach them to the handle element. This reuses the row's DnD
452	registration. Do not call `useSortable` again with the same row id: a handle mounted later
453	by virtualization would replace the row's registered DOM node.
454	
455	#### Keyboard reordering and accessibility
456	
457	`ReorderingProvider` supports keyboard row dragging.
458	Focus a drag handle, press Space or Enter to pick up the row, use the arrow keys to move it, and press
459	Space or Enter to drop it. Escape cancels the move.
460	Keyboard dragging applies only to rows; keyboard interactions with column headers remain unchanged.
461	
462	Use `accessibility` to customize dnd-kit's screen reader instructions, announcements, announcement
463	container, and focus restoration for both keyboard and pointer dragging.
464	When row and column providers are nested, they share the same DnD context and accessibility settings;
465	provider order does not matter.
466	
467	```tsx
468	<ReorderingProvider
469	  table={table}
470	  onReorder={handleReorder}
471	  accessibility={{
472	    screenReaderInstructions: {
473	      draggable:
474	        'Press Space to pick up a row, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, or Escape to cancel.',
475	    },
476	  }}
477	>
478	  <Table table={table} />
479	</ReorderingProvider>
480	```
481	
482	#### Column reordering
483	
484	Wrap the table with `ColumnReorderingProvider` to enable drag-and-drop reordering of columns by their headers.
485	
486	```tsx
487	import {ColumnReorderingProvider} from '@gravity-ui/table';
488	
489	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
490	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 100},
491	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
492	];
493	
494	const ColumnReorderingExample = () => {
495	  const table = useTable({
496	    columns,
497	    data,
498	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
499	  });
500	
501	  return (
502	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table}>
503	      <Table table={table} />
504	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
505	  );
506	};
507	```
508	
509	### Row and column reordering together
510	
511	Nest `ColumnReorderingProvider` and `ReorderingProvider` to enable both drag axes at once. The order of providers does not matter — they share a single dnd-kit context internally.
512	
513	```tsx
514	import type {ColumnReorderingProviderProps, ReorderingProviderProps} from '@gravity-ui/table';
515	import {ColumnReorderingProvider, ReorderingProvider, dragHandleColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
516	
517	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
518	  dragHandleColumn,
519	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
520	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
521	];
522	
523	const CombinedReorderingExample = () => {
524	  const [data, setData] = React.useState(initialData);
525	  const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
526	
527	  const table = useTable({
528	    columns,
529	    data,
530	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
531	    state: {columnOrder},
532	    onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
533	  });
534	
535	  const handleRowReorder = React.useCallback<
536	    NonNullable<ReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
537	  >(({draggedItemKey, baseItemKey}) => {
538	    // update data array
539	  }, []);
540	
541	  const handleColumnReorder = React.useCallback<
542	    NonNullable<ColumnReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
543	  >(({columnOrder}) => {
544	    setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
545	  }, []);
546	
547	  return (
548	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleColumnReorder}>
549	      <ReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleRowReorder}>
550	        <Table table={table} />
551	      </ReorderingProvider>
552	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
553	  );
554	};
555	```
556	
557	If you control `columnOrder` yourself (e.g. to persist it), pass `onReorder` and apply the resulting order:
558	
559	```tsx
560	const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
561	
562	const table = useTable({
563	  columns,
564	  data,
565	  state: {columnOrder},
566	  onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
567	});
568	
569	return (
570	  <ColumnReorderingProvider
571	    table={table}
572	    onReorder={({columnOrder}) => setColumnOrder(columnOrder)}
573	  >
574	    <Table table={table} />
575	  </ColumnReorderingProvider>
576	);
577	```
578	
579	CSS API:
580	
581	| CSS variable                                 | Default                       | Description                      |
582	| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
583	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-color` | `#4d8bff`                     | Color of the drop insertion line |
584	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-width` | `2px`                         | Width of the drop insertion line |
585	| `--gt-table-reordering-dragged-opacity`      | `0.4`                         | Opacity of the dragged column    |
586	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-background`         | `#fff`                        | Drag preview background          |
587	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-shadow`             | `0 3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` | Drag preview box-shadow          |
588	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-border-radius`      | `6px`                         | Drag preview border radius       |
589	
590	To forbid reordering a specific column, set `enableColumnReordering: false` in its column definition. Placeholder (grouped) columns are not draggable. Use `activationDistance` (default `8`) to tune how far the pointer must move before a drag starts, which keeps header clicks (like sorting) working.
591	
592	Pinned columns can be reordered too, but only among themselves: a column can be moved within the left-pinned group, the right-pinned group, or the center (non-pinned) group — it never crosses a pin boundary by dragging.
593	
594	```tsx
595	<ColumnReorderingProvider
596	  table={table}
597	  onReorder={({columnOrder, columnPinning, pinned}) => {
598	    if (pinned) {
599	      setColumnPinning(columnPinning);
600	    } else {
601	      setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
602	    }
603	  }}
604	>
605	  <Table table={table} />
606	</ColumnReorderingProvider>
607	```
608	
609	While dragging:
610	
611	- a floating preview of the column (its header plus the first rows) follows the pointer in a drag overlay;
612	- the dragged column becomes semi-transparent;
613	- a blue insertion line is drawn where the column will be dropped;
614	
615	```tsx
616	<ColumnReorderingProvider
617	  table={table}
618	  autoScroll
619	  dragOverlayRowCount={10}
620	  renderDragOverlay={({columnId}) => <CustomColumnPreview columnId={columnId} />}
621	>
622	  <Table table={table} />
623	</ColumnReorderingProvider>
624	```
625	
626	#### Virtualization
627	
628	Use if you want to use grid container as the scroll element (if you want to use window see window virtualization section). Be sure to set a fixed height on the container; otherwise, virtualization will not work.
629	
630	```tsx
631	import {useRowVirtualizer} from '@gravity-ui/table';
632	
633	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
634	  /* ... */
635	];
636	
637	const data: Person[] = [
638	  /* ... */
639	];
640	
641	const VirtualizationExample = () => {
642	  const table = useTable({
643	    columns,
644	    data,
645	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
646	  });
647	
648	  const containerRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
649	
650	  const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
651	    count: table.getRowModel().rows.length,
652	    estimateSize: () => 20,
653	    overscan: 5,
654	    getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
655	  });
656	
657	  return (
658	    <div ref={containerRef} style={{height: '500px', overflow: 'auto'}}>
659	      <Table table={table} rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer} />
660	    </div>
661	  );
662	};
663	```
664	
665	For tables that must stay covered during continuous bidirectional scrolling, enable the adaptive
666	direct-DOM mode and use stable semantic keys. The same key must identify a row before and after an
667	immutable reorder or a tree reparent:
668	
669	```tsx
670	import {getColumnAwareRowOverscan} from '@gravity-ui/table';
671	
672	const rows = table.getRowModel().rows;
673	const columnCount = table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length;
674	
675	const getItemKey = React.useCallback(
676	  (index: number) => rows[index]?.id ?? `missing:${index}`,
677	  [rows],
678	);
679	
680	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
681	  adaptiveFlushSync: true,
682	  count: rows.length,
683	  directDomUpdates: true,
684	  directDomUpdatesMode: 'position',
685	  estimateSize: () => 40,
686	  getItemKey,
687	  getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
688	  overscan: getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount),
689	});
690	```
691	
692	`adaptiveFlushSync` keeps a warm mounted range and synchronously fills only an uncovered visible
693	range. `directDomUpdates` lets the virtualizer update row positions and the body size without a
694	React render for every scroll notification. Use `position` for table rows unless transforms are
695	required by the surrounding layout. Keep `getRowId` and `getItemKey` stable, and set `count` from
696	the current flattened row model after expanding, collapsing, reordering, or reparenting rows.
697	An arbitrary custom `rangeExtractor` remains authoritative and disables adaptive window planning.
698	
699	`getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount, options?)` reduces the base row overscan as the number
700	of columns grows. By default, it divides a 240-cell budget by the column count, rounds down,
701	and clamps the result to 4–24 rows. Use `table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length` to exclude hidden
702	columns and include pinned columns. The helper works with both `useRowVirtualizer` and
703	`useWindowRowVirtualizer`; you can still pass an explicit numeric `overscan` instead.
704	
705	Tune the budget and bounds for your cell rendering cost. If your application virtualizes columns,
706	set `renderedColumnLimit` to the maximum number of columns rendered per row, including pinned
707	columns; the helper caps the supplied column count at this value:
708	
709	```tsx
710	const overscan = getColumnAwareRowOverscan(table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length, {
711	  renderedColumnLimit: 16,
712	  cellBudget: 320,
713	  minOverscan: 4,
714	  maxOverscan: 20,
715	});
716	```
717	
718	The result is a base row overscan, not a strict limit on mounted rows or cells. Visible rows are
719	rendered in addition to the overscan, and adaptive scrolling can extend the mounted range.
720	All helper inputs must be non-negative safe integers, and `maxOverscan` must be at least
721	`minOverscan`; invalid values throw a `RangeError`. Zero columns are treated as one for the calculation.
722	
723	`BaseTable.canDeferOffscreenCellContent` is an additional opt-in for very wide adaptive tables.
724	Return `true` only for passive cell content whose delayed mount cannot change geometry, focus,
725	accessibility, or application state. Custom rows, group rows, pinned cells, and interactive or
726	side-effectful content should remain eager.
727	
728	With the default adaptive range extractor, `BaseTable` pins the active dragged row automatically.
729	A custom range extractor is responsible for retaining that row itself. If you use reordering with
730	a non-adaptive virtualizer, keep the same semantic `getItemKey` contract and pass the
731	`rangeExtractor` option:
732	
733	```tsx
734	import {getVirtualRowRangeExtractor} from '@gravity-ui/table';
735	
736	// ...
737	
738	const tableRef = React.useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null);
739	
740	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
741	  // ...
742	  rangeExtractor: getVirtualRowRangeExtractor(tableRef.current),
743	});
744	
745	return (
746	  <TableWithReordering
747	    ref={tableRef}
748	    table={table}
749	    rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer}
750	    onReorder={handleReorder}
751	  />
752	);
753	```
754	
755	#### Window virtualization
756	
757	Use if you want to use window as the scroll element
758	
759	```tsx
760	import {useWindowRowVirtualizer} from '@gravity-ui/table';
761	
762	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
763	  /* ... */
764	];
765	
766	const data: Person[] = [
767	  /* ... */
768	];
769	
770	const WindowVirtualizationExample = () => {
771	  const table = useTable({
772	    columns,
773	    data,
774	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
775	  });
776	
777	  const bodyRef = React.useRef<HTMLTableSectionElement>(null);
778	
779	  const rowVirtualizer = useWindowRowVirtualizer({
780	    count: table.getRowModel().rows.length,
781	    estimateSize: () => 20,
782	    overscan: 5,
783	    scrollMargin: bodyRef.current?.offsetTop ?? 0,
784	  });
785	
786	  return <Table table={table} rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer} bodyRef={bodyRef} />;
787	};
788	```
789	
790	#### Resizing
791	
792	```tsx
793	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
794	  /* ... */
795	];
796	
797	const data: Person[] = [
798	  /* ... */
799	];
800	
801	const ResizingDemo = () => {
802	  const table = useTable({
803	    columns,
804	    data,
805	    enableColumnResizing: true,
806	    columnResizeMode: 'onChange',
807	  });
808	
809	  return <Table table={table} />;
810	};
811	```
812	
813	#### Column settings
814	
815	Set `enableReset` to `true` to show the settings popup's Reset button (hidden by default).
816	It restores column visibility and order from the table's `initialState`. Reset changes
817	the popup draft; press Apply to save it. Without an `initialState`, Reset shows all
818	columns in their definition order.
819	The optional `onSettingsReset` callback receives that restored visibility and column order
820	when Reset is clicked, before the draft is applied.
821	
822	```tsx
823	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
824	  // ...other columns
825	  {
826	    id: 'settings_column_id',
827	    header: ({table}) => <TableSettings table={table} />,
828	    meta: {
829	      hideInSettings: false, // Optional. Allows to hide this column from settings popover
830	      titleInSettings: 'ReactNode', // Optional. Overrides header field for settings popover (if you need different content for header and settings popover)
831	    },
832	  }, // or you can use function getSettingsColumn
833	];
834	
835	const data: Person[] = [
836	  /* ... */
837	];
838	
839	const TableSettingsDemo = () => {
840	  const [columnVisibility, onColumnVisibilityChange] = React.useState<VisibilityState>({
841	    // for outside control and initial state
842	    column_id: false, // for hidding by default
843	  });
844	  const [columnOrder, onColumnOrderChange] = React.useState<string[]>([
845	    /* leaf columns ids */
846	  ]); // for outside control and initial state
847	
848	  // Alternative variant to get state, callbacks, and set on setting apply callbacks - using useTableSettings hook:
849	  // const {state, callbacks} = useTableSettings({initialVisibility: {}, initialOrder: []})
850	
851	  const table = useTable({
852	    columns,
853	    data,
854	    state: {
855	      columnVisibility,
856	      columnOrder,
857	    },
858	    onColumnVisibilityChange,
859	    onColumnOrderChange,
860	  });
861	
862	  return <Table table={table} />;
863	};
864	```
865	
866	Learn more about the table and the column resizing properties in the react-table [docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/api/features/column-sizing)
867	
868	## Guides
869	
870	- [Migration Guide: From Table (@gravity-ui/uikit) to Table (@gravity-ui/table)](./guides/migration-from-uikit-table/migration-from-uikit-table.md)
871	- [Руководство по миграции с Table (@gravity-ui/uikit) на Table (@gravity-ui/table)](./guides/migration-from-uikit-table/migration-from-uikit-table-ru.md)
872	
873	## Components
874	
875	- [BaseTable](./components/BaseTable.md) — The unstyled, low-level table renderer — renders a useTable instance as raw <table> markup without Gravity UI styling, for full visual control.
876	
877	## Hooks
878	
879	- [useColumnsAutoSize](./hooks/useColumnsAutoSize.md) — A React hook that automatically calculates column widths based on measured content, supporting primitives and React nodes, accessorKey/accessorFn columns, custom cell renderers, and respect for predefined or user-resized widths.

1 # AsideHeader 2 3 `AsideHeader` is provided a flexible and customizable navigation experience within your application. 4 Users can easily customize the appearance of the sidebar to match their branding colors also to add personalized links, icons that cater specifically to their application's functionality. 5 6 The component offers a robust solution for creating intuitive and visually appealing navigation systems, enhancing user experience while providing the flexibility to adapt to various use cases. 7 8 ```ts 9 import {AsideHeader} from '@gravity-ui/navigation'; 10 ``` 11 12 ## Appearance 13 14 ### State 15 16 The component has two possible states: collapsed, expanded. 17 Уou can manage between states using `compact`, `onChangeCompact` props and also hide button with `hideCollapseButton`. 18 19 Collapse and expansion animate the sidebar width, item positions, and selection surfaces together. 20 Titles are laid out at the target width and revealed during expansion, without rewrapping on each 21 frame or a second layout change at the end. Clicking the control again reverses from the currently 22 displayed positions. The `compact` state and callbacks always describe the requested target state. 23 Users who prefer reduced motion receive an immediate layout change. 24 25 All built-in horizontal separators, including `type: 'divider'` items in header, menu, footer, 26 and nested groups, resize with the sidebar while preserving their local spacing. 27 28 The current-item transition follows changes to `compact`: when a selected child 29 becomes represented by its group or **More**, one background moves between those rows. It also 30 supports reversing an unfinished transition. Ordinary page selection remains immediate, and 31 quick-access highlight settings and the theme's selection transparency are preserved. A current 32 change during this movement restores native highlighting while the layout continues animating. 33 Ambiguous selections retain existing native highlighting; reduced motion switches immediately. 34 35 ### Disabling compact transitions 36 37 Set `compactTransition={false}` on `AsideHeader` or `PageLayout` (default: `true`). 38 Aside and content widths, custom background width, row and divider geometry, current-item 39 highlighting, and the offset of an open Drawer immediately follow the target `compact` state. 40 Disabling the flag during a transition finishes it immediately and releases transition resources. 41 Re-enabling it without changing `compact` does not animate; simultaneous updates use the new flag. 42 Children stay mounted. `PageLayoutAside` and `AsideFallback` inherit the layout setting. 43 44 Hover effects, independent Drawer opening/closing, and the opacity effects of the footer divider 45 and custom scrollbar are preserved. The existing `prefers-reduced-motion` behavior is unchanged. 46 47 ```tsx 48 49 50 51 52 {children} 53 54 ``` 55 56 ### Collapse button (v7) 57 58 The collapse button sits at the aside edge beside the last visible `FooterItem`. The row keeps its 59 own action and menu; in expanded mode it reserves 24 px for the button. In compact mode, hovering 60 anywhere in the aside or over the button, or focusing the button from the keyboard, reveals the 61 control. The selected row's built-in tooltip is suppressed in compact mode even when `enableTooltip={true}`. With no 62 visible `FooterItem`, a blank bottom row provides the same control. `hideCollapseButton` removes 63 the control, reserved space, and blank row. 64 65 The button remains keyboard accessible and retains focus when toggled. `expandTitle` and 66 `collapseTitle` set its accessible name. `compactTransition={false}` disables its geometry 67 transitions while preserving hover appearance; reduced motion disables both. 68 69 While the aside animates towards compact the button stays hidden, so its collapsed appearance never 70 lands on an aside that is still at its expanded width; hover reveals it once the layout settles. A 71 keyboard-focused button stays visible throughout. Expanding is unaffected — the button is visible 72 for the whole transition. 73 74 In compact mode the button is a 20 px tab attached to the outside of the aside edge: concave 75 fillets merge it into the edge and a single 1 px outline runs around it, so the vertical divider 76 stays unbroken. The tab rests behind the aside edge and slides out from under it on hover or 77 keyboard focus; it never fades. Its layer is a 20 px strip outside the aside edge at 78 `calc(var(--gn-aside-header-z-index, 100) + 1)`, clipped while compact; the tab extends 20 px over 79 the edge of open All pages and custom `panelItems` Drawers. Clicking the tab changes `compact` and 80 keeps the panel open. Its transparent layer does not 81 intercept clicks outside the button. Consumer z-index settings determine custom stacking; portaled 82 Popups (including `asideRef` with `right-end`) may cover the tab and retain their normal position 83 and behavior. The tab fill follows the collapsed aside background, then the general aside 84 background, then the theme background. Matching an arbitrary `customBackground` is not guaranteed. 85 The outline follows the vertical divider color (`--gn-aside-header-divider-vertical-color`); 86 `--gn-aside-header-collapse-button-border-color` overrides it for the tab alone. The expanded 87 button keeps no outline. 88 89 In v7, `collapseButtonWrapper` decorates the edge control. Move any full-width additional content 90 previously rendered by this wrapper into `renderFooter`: 91 92 ```tsx 93 {button}} 95 renderFooter={({compact}) => ( 96 <> 97
Additional footer content
98 99 100 )} 101 /> 102 ``` 103 104 `PageLayoutAside` must participate directly in the flex layout of `PageLayout`. React components, 105 Fragments, Context providers, and Suspense are supported without extra DOM boxes. If a consumer 106 needs a DOM wrapper, give it `display: contents`; an ordinary block wrapper is unsupported. 107 The library does not change consumer wrapper styles automatically. 108 109 ```tsx 110 111
112 113
114 {children} 115 116 ``` 117 118 ### Menu density 119 120 Use `menuDensity="compact"` to reduce the aside width, item height, icon size, spacing, and corner 121 radius without changing how the navigation behaves. Density is independent from the collapsed or 122 expanded state controlled by `compact`, so both properties can be combined. 123 124 ```tsx 125 131 ``` 132 133 The default value is `default`, which preserves the previous dimensions. Compact density reduces 134 menu, subheader, and footer item icons; it does not resize the standard 24 px logo icon. 135 With the advanced layout pattern, pass `menuDensity` to `PageLayout`; `PageLayoutAside` inherits 136 the normalized value from context. 137 138 ### Top decoration 139 140 Navigation highlights top section with Logo and Subheader items using `headerDecoration` props. 141 142 ### Section dividers 143 144 `hideSectionDividers` hides the header/footer separators (including the collapsed header decoration SVG) and their spacing toward the menu. Header background, outer spacing, and separators inside the menu/Quick Access are preserved. 145 146 With `hideSectionDividers=true`, indicators appear at the menu scroll edges only while content is hidden beyond that edge: bottom at the start, both in the middle, top at the end, neither without overflow. They do not restore spacing. With `false`, the existing footer separator remains visible whenever the menu overflows, including at the end. The Quick Access separator stays inside the scrolling content and can coexist with these indicators. Setting `--gn-aside-header-divider-horizontal-color: transparent` also hides the scroll indicators. 147 148 The property is supported by `AsideHeader` and `PageLayoutAside`. `AsideFallback` supports hiding separators and spacing only: it has no scrollable menu and does not render scroll-edge indicators. 149 150 ### Custom background 151 152 The component supports specific themization cases, e.g. image on background or splitting sections by color — using `customBackground`, `customBackgroundClassName` props. 153 154 ## Sections 155 156 Navigation includes 3 parts: the top, the middle and the bottom. These sections are similar with a few variations of possibilities based on frequency user cases. 157 **Important note**: A user manages the state of the elements. 158 159 ### The Top 160 161 The section usually contains general elements for all site pages and includes the logo and the elements below it. Clickable logo can be useful for a quick navigation to the home page, if necessary the element (e.g. search, catalogue) is placed under it. 162 163 ### The Middle (menuItems) 164 165 The main section usually depends on context of the page — one of examples using navigation on the multipage sites. 166 The elements will collapse into three dots if there is no vertical space by default. 167 168 Navigation elements can be in one of two states: collapsed (isCollapsed), where only the icon is visible, and expanded. There is some space for customization of the entire item through a wrapper. 169 170 With additional configuration via `AllPages` users can further customize menu to their preference by hiding unnecessary items. This brings in a new state for items - `hidden`. Compression should go into scroll on the 142 container of the wide thing only. 143 144 For a full-height app frame: root `height: 100vh` (+ a sane `min-height`), 145 panels `flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto` — the panel scrolls, not the 146 document. 147 148 --- 149 150 ## Theming 151 152 ### Styles + fonts are required; order matters 153 154 ❌ **Incorrect** — missing imports, or theme before base: 155 156 ```tsx 157 import './theme.css'; // before styles.css → gets overwritten 158 import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'; 159 // no styles.css, no fonts.css → components render unstyled 160 ``` 161 162 ✓ **Correct**: 163 164 ```tsx 165 import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css'; // fonts first 166 import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css'; // then base 167 import './theme.css'; // custom ALWAYS after styles.css 168 import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'; 169 ``` 170 171 **Why:** without `styles.css` + `fonts.css` imported once at the entry point, 172 every component renders unstyled. A custom theme file imported *before* 173 `styles.css` is overwritten by it in the cascade — custom always comes after. 174 175 ### `theme` takes five values — no `"default"` or `"auto"` 176 177 ❌ `` 178 ❌ `` 179 ✓ `` / `"dark"` / `"light-hc"` / `"dark-hc"` 180 ✓ `` (resolves to light/dark from OS preference) 181 182 ### Branding means a full token set, on both themes — never 2–4 tokens 183 184 ❌ **Incorrect** — partial override: 185 186 ```css 187 .g-root { --g-color-base-brand: #007AFF; } 188 ``` 189 190 ✓ **Correct** — override the full brand group, per theme: 191 192 ```css 193 .g-root_theme_light { 194 --g-color-base-brand: #007AFF; 195 --g-color-base-brand-hover: #0066D6; 196 --g-color-base-selection: rgba(0, 122, 255, 0.05); 197 --g-color-base-selection-hover: rgba(0, 122, 255, 0.1); 198 --g-color-line-brand: #007AFF; 199 --g-color-text-brand: #007AFF; 200 --g-color-text-brand-contrast: #FFFFFF; /* required: text on brand bg */ 201 --g-color-text-link: #007AFF; 202 --g-color-text-link-hover: #0066D6; 203 } 204 .g-root_theme_dark { 205 /* different values — dark usually needs a brighter brand */ 206 --g-color-base-brand: #2E8BFF; 207 /* … same set, dark-tuned … */ 208 } 209 ``` 210 211 **Why:** the semantic layer has many tokens pointing at "brand" — selection, 212 focus, links, the contrast text on a brand background. Override only 213 `--g-color-base-brand` and you get a UI where the button is branded but 214 selection, links and focus rings are still the default accent. Provide the full 215 set, and provide it for *each* theme you support (dark themes usually need a 216 brighter brand than light). Forgetting `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` makes 217 text on a brand button unreadable. 218 219 Better than hand-writing: generate the full set with the 220 [Themer](https://gravity-ui.com/themer) web tool or 221 [`@gravity-ui/uikit-themer`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit-themer) — both 222 recalculate the dependent palette from a single base color. 223 224 ### A section `ThemeProvider` with no provider above it themes the whole page 225 226 ❌ **Incorrect** — a dark widget mounted where no `ThemeProvider` (or v8 227 `Provider`) wraps it: an embedded widget, a micro-frontend, a separate React 228 root: 229 230 ```tsx 231 {/* no provider above → writes to document.body */} 232 233 234 ``` 235 236 ✓ **Correct**: 237 238 ```tsx 239 240 241 242 ``` 243 244 **Why:** only the outermost `ThemeProvider` writes the theme class to 245 `document.body` — globally, last-wins. One nested inside another 246 `ThemeProvider` (or a v8 `Provider`) is always scoped, with or without the prop, 247 so a dark section inside the app needs no `scoped`. With no provider above, 248 `scoped` renders a dedicated `
` around the 249 children *and* updates the theme React context (so `useTheme` inside the 250 section sees the section's theme). For a CSS-only region without context, apply 251 the class manually: `
`. 252 253 ### Controls on a brand/colored background: fixed contrast, both themes 254 255 ❌ **Incorrect** — default button on a brand-colored hero: 256 257 ```tsx 258
259 {/* default view follows theme → low contrast on bright bg */} 260
261 ``` 262 263 ✓ **Correct** — use a `*-contrast` view, which is built for a contrast 264 background, or scope a CSS override fixing contrast for both themes: 265 266 ```tsx 267
268 {/* also outlined-contrast, flat-contrast */} 269
270 ``` 271 272 **Why:** a brand-colored fill is usually the *same* color in light and dark 273 (it's a fill, not a themed surface), so the control on top should keep a fixed 274 contrast in both themes rather than lightening/darkening with the theme. 275 `normal-contrast` / `outlined-contrast` / `flat-contrast` do exactly that. 276 Do **not** reach for `raised` here — its surface is themed (light in light, 277 dark in dark), so it does not hold contrast on a fixed fill. If no `*-contrast` 278 view fits, override the component's CSS API (`--g-button-background-color`, 279 `--g-button-text-color`, …) scoped to the section, with contrast values for 280 both themes. This is distinct from `--g-color-text-brand-contrast`, which is 281 about text on a *brand button* (`view="action"`). 282 283 ### Customization ladder — descend only when there's no higher handle 284 285 When you need to change how a Gravity UI component looks, try in this order: 286 287 1. **Global tokens** (`--g-*` semantic tokens / theme) — change the look 288 everywhere by changing the token, not components one by one. 289 2. **Component's own CSS API** (`--g-button-*`, `--g-card-border-radius`, 290 `--g-text-input-*`, …) — scoped to the wrapper / class of the spot you're 291 changing. Check the component's README for the variables it exposes. 292 3. **A narrow, flagged hack** — a custom class on a specific internal element, 293 with a comment "hack on internal classes, pinned to version ", and a note 294 to upstream it. Only after confirming step 1 and 2 don't expose a handle. 295 4. **NEVER** broad structural matches: `[class*='…']` or ID selectors against 296 internal markup. Such an override is written against one specific DOM 297 structure and breaks silently when it changes. 298 299 **Why:** a `[class*='…']` override that worked yesterday breaks tomorrow when 300 the component adds a wrapper or renames an internal class — and you won't get a 301 type error, just a visually broken layout. Always start at the top of the 302 ladder; descend one rung only when the rung above has no handle. 303 304 --- 305 306 ## Color & shape 307 308 ### Use semantic tokens, never raw hex or private tokens 309 310 ❌ `color: #1677FF` 311 ❌ `background: var(--g-color-private-blue-500)` 312 ✓ `color: var(--g-color-text-link)` 313 ✓ `background: var(--g-color-base-brand)` 314 315 **Why:** Gravity UI's color system is two-layered. The *private* layer 316 (`--g-color-private--`) is the raw palette — an implementation 317 detail that can change, never reference it directly. The *semantic* layer 318 (`--g-color-{group}-{role}`) encodes intent and is theme-aware. Use it: 319 320 - backgrounds/fills: `--g-color-base-*` (`base-background`, `base-brand`, 321 `base-generic`, `base-danger-*`, …) 322 - text/icons: `--g-color-text-*` (`text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-hint`, 323 `text-brand`, `text-link`, …) 324 - borders/lines: `--g-color-line-*` (`line-generic`, `line-brand`, `line-focus`, 325 `line-danger`) 326 - effects: `--g-color-sfx-*` (`sfx-shadow`, `sfx-veil`, `sfx-fade`) 327 328 For text on a brand/colored background, use `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` 329 (not the plain brand color — it has no contrast guarantee). 330 331 ### Border radius uses a token, never a hard-coded `px` 332 333 ❌ `border-radius: 8px` 334 ✓ `border-radius: var(--g-border-radius-m)` 335 336 **Why:** the scale is `--g-border-radius-{xs|s|m|l|xl}`. Components expose 337 their own radius variable on the same scale (`--g-button-border-radius`, 338 `--g-card-border-radius`, `--g-modal-border-radius`, …) so you can tune one 339 component without moving the global scale. Use a token, always. 340 341 --- 342 343 ## Component-prop traps (cross-cutting) 344 345 ### `Button` uses `view`, not `variant` / `color` 346 347 ❌ `

events.content:
`BaseGroupHeader` is a full-width group header row (colSpan = visibleCells.length) with built-in chevron toggle, title (via getGroupTitle), and count (row.subRows.length). This is the clean grouping approach:

- data: `OrderGroup[]` = `{id: status, status, items: Order[]}`
- `getSubRows: (item) => item.items`
- `enableExpanding: true`, `expanded` state
- `getIsGroupHeaderRow: (row) => row.getCanExpand()` — wait, when expanded state... `getCanExpand()` returns true for rows with subRows. Good. But then the leaf rows' cells render normally.
- `getGroupTitle: (row) => status label`
- Selection: `selectionColumn` + `useRowSelectionFixedHandler`. Note the group header row is rendered as a single colspan cell — so the group row checkbox won't render (group header replaces all cells). With `useRowSelectionFixedHandler`, leaf-row selection state determines group... but the group header row shows no checkbox. Hmm. The doc says "To use grouping with selection, use useRowSelectionFixedHandler hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong." That's for the tree-style grouping (TreeExpandableCell) where group rows render as regular rows with cells. But with BaseGroupHeader (colspan row), there's no checkbox on group rows at all.

Two approaches:
A. Use `BaseGroupHeader` full-width group rows (colspan), selection only on leaf rows. Simpler and looks like a proper grouped grid. `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` is for fixing parent checkbox state — with no parent checkbox, not strictly needed, but selection state via `rowSelection` on leaf ids still works fine.

B. Tree-style: group rows render as regular rows with TreeExpandableCell in the first data column, plus checkboxes on group rows, requiring `useRowSelectionFixedHandler`.

Option A is cleaner for "группировка строк по статусу заказа" — the group header spans the whole width showing status + count. Leaf rows show checkboxes. No need for fixed handler. But wait — there's a subtlety: the header "select all" checkbox selects all rows including group rows. `table.getIsAllRowsSelected()` with subRows... TanStack handles selection propagation to subRows automatically when `enableSubRowSelection` (default true). The standard selectionColumn works.

However the docs explicitly recommend `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` when grouping with selection — due to TanStack issue #4878 (parent row checkbox state wrong). With approach A (colspan group header), group rows don't render checkboxes, so the issue doesn't surface. But selecting "all" via header checkbox: with grouped data, getToggleAllRowsSelectedHandler selects all leaf + group rows; leaf rows render checkboxes fine.

I'll go with approach A. Simple, robust, and matches the package's intended grouped rendering.

One more consideration: with grouping, do I need `getExpandedRowModel`? TanStack: for expanding subRows, you need `getExpandedRowModel: getExpandedRowModel()` from '@tanstack/react-table'... Actually useTable from @gravity-ui/table might include it by default. Let me check useTable.js.

Also, the table i18n: @gravity-ui/table uses @gravity-ui/i18n (installed). Table text (like "rows selected"?) mostly none. Fine.

Now design the app:

**Files:**
1. `src/main.tsx` — check current content first.

6. Maybe `src/styles.css` — small layout CSS using tokens.

Page switching: keep `page` state in App; menuItems built from it with `current` flags; renderContent renders the active page.

**Table details:**
- Types: 
```ts
interface Order { id: string; number: string; customer: string; date: string; amount: number; items: number; address: string; status: OrderStatus }
interface OrderGroup { id: string; status: OrderStatus; items: Order[] }
type TableItem = OrderGroup | Order
```
- Columns (`ColumnDef<TableItem>[]`):
  - selectionColumn (as ColumnDef<TableItem>)
  - id: accessorKey 'number' → header 'Заказ'; cell: for group rows show nothing? Group rows render as BaseGroupHeader colspan, so leaf-only values fine. But wait: for the group row, cells aren't rendered at all (colspan replaces them). So plain accessor columns work. 
  - customer 'Клиент'
  - status 'Статус' — for leaf rows render Label. Group rows don't render cells. accessorFn: (item) => 'status' in item && !('items' in item)... hmm, leaf Order has status; group also has status. Fine — accessor just used for value extraction; group rows' cells not rendered anyway.
  - date 'Дата'
  - items 'Товары'
  - amount 'Сумма' — format ₽
  - address 'Адрес доставки'
- With `accessorKey`, TanStack requires data rows to have those keys; group rows lack them (number, customer...) — fine since their cells aren't rendered.
- Column ids: default from accessorKey.
- `enableColumnReordering: false` on selection column? selectionColumn likely has that meta already... The docs say to forbid reordering set `enableColumnReordering: false` in column def. The built-in selectionColumn — let me check whether it sets it. Quick check of selectionColumn.js.

State:
- rowSelection + setRowSelection
- expanded (default expanded: true? ExpandedState — pass `true` to expand all by default)
- columnOrder + onColumnOrderChange via ColumnReorderingProvider onReorder → setColumnOrder

Table options:
```ts
const table = useTable({
  columns, data,
  getRowId: (item) => item.id,
  enableExpanding: true,
  getSubRows: (item) => ('items' in item ? item.items : undefined),
  enableRowSelection: true,
  enableMultiRowSelection: true,
  onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
  state: {rowSelection, expanded, columnOrder},
  onExpandedChange: setExpanded,
  onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
})
```
Render:
```tsx
<ColumnReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={({columnOrder}) => setColumnOrder(columnOrder)}>
  <Table table={table} getGroupTitle={getGroupTitle} getIsGroupHeaderRow={(row) => row.getCanExpand()} />
</ColumnReorderingProvider>

getGroupTitle: `(row) => \`${statusMeta.title}\`` — BaseGroupHeader already shows count via row.subRows.length. Add total sum maybe: title can include sum. Keep it: status title. The count is automatic.

Row ids: group id = status; leaf id = order id. Unique ✓.

Row selection with grouping: with subRows, selecting group row (via header select-all) cascades. Leaf checkboxes fine. The `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` is needed only for parent-row checkboxes (tree style). Group header rows here have no checkbox. OK.

Also add sorting? Not requested. Skip to keep focused. Maybe add sorting on date/amount — not required; skip.

Selected-count indicator: show "Выбрано: N" text above the table — demonstrates selection. N = number of selected leaf rows. rowSelection keys include group ids when selecting all. Count leaf ids only: `table.getSelectedRowModel().rows.filter(r => !r.getCanExpand()).length`... getSelectedRowModel returns flat rows incl groups. Filter `'number' in r.original`.

Key finding: `gn-aside-header__content` has `width: calc(100% - var(--gn-aside-header-size))` and the aside is `position: sticky; height: 100vh`. The root `.AsideHeader` is height: 100%. The content region grows with the page; the whole page scrolls (document). So the layout model: document scrolls, sidebar sticky. For the table area, I'll make the page a column with `min-height: 100vh` (or just natural) and let the table area scroll internally with a bounded height: `height: calc(100vh - padding)`. Simpler: `.orders-page { height: 100vh; display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding; box-sizing: border-box; }` — since content region starts at top:0 (no top alert), 100vh is right. The table wrapper gets `flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto` → internal scroll + stickyHeader works.

Now write all files.

- **`src/pages/StubPage.tsx`** — заглушки для остальных разделов
- **`src/data/orders.ts`** — 48 мок-заказов по 5 статусам

## Боковая навигация (`@gravity-ui/navigation` → `AsideHeader`)

- Разделы **Главная, Пользователи, Заказы, Настройки** с иконками из `@gravity-ui/icons` (`House`, `Persons`, `ShoppingCart`, `Gear` — имена проверены в установленной версии, не выдуманы)
- Сворачивание в иконки: контролируемые `compact` + `onChangeCompact` (встроенная кнопка collapse)
- В футере — `FooterItem` с переключением светлой/тёмной темы (`Moon`/`Sun` → `ThemeProvider`)

## Таблица заказов (`@gravity-ui/table`, TanStack-based)

- **Выделение строк** — чекбоксы (uikit `Checkbox`, включая «выбрать все» в шапке), счётчик «Выбрано заказов: N». Осознанно без range-selection (Shift+click): для вложенных/сгруппированных строк он undefined behavior по докам пакета
- **Перетаскивание колонок** — `ColumnReorderingProvider` с контролируемым `columnOrder` (колонку выбора зафиксировал через `enableColumnReordering: false`)
- **Группировка по статусу** — иерархические данные (`getSubRows`), полноширинные групповые шапки `BaseGroupHeader` со сворачиванием, названием статуса, суммой и счётчиком заказов; группы по умолчанию развёрнуты
- Бонус: `stickyHeader`, статусы — uikit `Label` с семантическими темами, форматирование сумм/дат через `Intl` (ru-RU)

## По ходу работы

- Установил `@gravity-ui/navigation@7.1.3` и `@gravity-ui/table@1.25.0` (версии 8.x navigation требуют uikit ^8, а в проекте uikit 7.43) + peer-зависимости, и закрепил `@tanstack/react-table@^8` (в корень попал несовместимый v9)
- Поймал расхождение доки и установленной версии: `SelectionCheckbox` в этой версии не экспортируется из корня пакета — заменил на uikit `Checkbox` по задокументированному паттерну

Что `tsc` не покрывает (проверьте глазами при запуске `npm run dev`): внешний вид в обеих темах, поведение на узких (~375px) и широких (~1400px) экранах — таблица при этом скроллится горизонтально внутри своего контейнера, сайдбар остаётся на месте.
